item.title: Iranian Jordanian FMs hold phone talks discuss regional developments
item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi and Jordanian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ayman Safadi held a phone conversation on Tuesday morning to discuss regional developments. During the conversation, Araghchi outlined Iran’s positions on regional developments and stressed the need for Islamic countries and the international community to take serious action to counter the continued genocide and expansionism of the occupying Zionist regime. Recalling the devastating consequences of the US and Israeli military aggression against Iran for the region and the world, the Iranian foreign minister emphasized that restoring security to the region requires an end to the United States’ aggressive and interventionist actions, as well as containing the Zionist regime’s expansionism and warmongering. Araghchi also condemned the terrorist attack on a church in southern Jordan and expressed his condolences to the families of those killed in the incident. The foreign ministers of the two countries underscored the importance of making use of diplomacy and continuing political consultations to safeguard peace and stability in the region.

item.description: Iranian Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi, reacting to French President Emmanuel Macron’s contradictory statements on Iran’s nuclear activities, wrote on X that Macron had pledged in 2018 that France would not withdraw from the JCPOA because it had signed the deal, but now claims to have always opposed any nuclear activity in Iran. “Stick to your own account, Mr. President!” Araghchi wrote.

item.title: Baqaei: US negotiating approach not Iranians’ religious beliefs blocks diplomacy
item.description: Iranian Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei wrote on X that the US negotiating approach, characterized by unilateral demands, failure to honor commitments, and reliance on coercion, is the real obstacle to rational negotiations with Iran, not Iranians’ religious beliefs. He urged Washington to understand Iran’s strategic interests and legitimate security concerns and address its own record of breaching commitments. "What does the American administration's failure to respect its diplomatic commitments and its addiction to force and pressure have to do with the "religious beliefs" of Iranians?! Faith does not preclude 'rationality', just as secularism does not guarantee wisdom. What makes "rational negotiations" impossible is not "Iran’s religious beliefs", but America’s negotiating behavior, which amounts to little more than one-sided dictation rather than genuine diplomacy. You cannot demand concessions while refusing reciprocity, dictate terms while ignoring the other side’s legitimate interests, and expect a lasting agreement. Stop making ideologically driven assumptions about Iranians’ religious beliefs and start understanding Iran’s strategic interests and legitimate security concerns. And above all, instead of accusing others, address your own record of broken promises."

item.title: Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda meets Foreign Minister Araghchi
item.description: Reza Nourian, the newly appointed ambassador of the Islamic Republic of Iran to Uganda, met with Foreign Minister Seyed Abbas Araghchi before departing for his post and outlined his proposed plan to expand bilateral cooperation between Tehran and Kampala in various fields. The foreign minister, while wishing Nourian success in his mission in Uganda, stressed the need to make use of existing capacities and opportunities to increase trade exchanges and strengthen relations and cooperation in areas of mutual interest, particularly in the political, economic and agricultural sectors. Before his appointment as Iran’s new ambassador to Uganda, Nourian served as deputy director of the Department for Cultural Cooperation and NGOs at the Foreign Ministry’s Center for Public Diplomacy.
